transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well... ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself. I find myself crying over little things, like the potluck lists. And I get all worked up about phone calls I used to handle easy. I've even started missing church planning things that I never, ever would have missed before. I just knew I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Since your friend passed away, have you found yourself longing for them or feeling preoccupied with thoughts of them?

No, I wouldn't say I'm longing for her or, you know, constantly thinking about her. It's more just... when something reminds me of her, like those potluck lists, it just hits me hard. But I'm not sitting around preoccupied with thoughts of her all day. It's just the everyday things that are harder now.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel depressed all day long. It's not like a dark cloud hanging over me from morning till night. It's really just... like I said, when things get overwhelming or I get reminded of her. But most of the day, no, I'm not just sitting around feeling down.
Did these problems start within 3 months after your friend passed away?

Yes, it did. My friend died just about a month ago, and it was really only after that sudden loss that I started falling apart with the church planning and getting so worked up. So yes, it definitely started within that time frame.
Have these changes made it hard for you to carry out your usual responsibilities?

Yes, they have. I've actually had to let some of the other church members take over the phone calls, the lists, and even parts of the luncheon. I'm just... I'm not keeping up with it all the way I always did before.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when they are not related to your friend's death?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about getting the church things done because I'm behind, but I don't just sit around worrying about everything under the sun. It's really just tied to missing her and feeling overwhelmed by the things we used to do together. I wouldn't say I'm an excessive worrier about other things.
Do these reactions feel stronger than you would have expected for yourself after your friend's death?

I'm really not sure about that. I mean... I've never lost a friend this close before, so I don't really know what to expect of myself. I just know it's been really hard to get through the days and do the church things we used to do together. But as for whether it's stronger than it should be... I honestly couldn't tell you. I just know I'm struggling with it.
Does the intensity of how upset you feel seem out of proportion to what you would expect after your friend's death?

Well, like I was just saying a moment ago... I really don't have a way to measure that. I don't know what "in proportion" would even look like for something like this. I just know that I miss her terribly and it's throwing my days off. I honestly couldn't tell you if it's more intense than it's supposed to be.
Would you say this has caused you a lot of emotional distress?

I'm not really sure if I would use the word distress, exactly. I mean... I'm just very sad. Like I said, I miss her terribly and it's making my days hard to get through, especially with the church work. But as far as "emotional distress"... I don't know. I just know I'm grieving her.
Because of this, have you been less able to handle your usual church responsibilities than you normally would?

Yes, I have. I've actually had to let some of the other church members take over for me. They've been handling the phone calls and the lists, and... well, even parts of the luncheon. I'm just not keeping up with it all the way I always did before.
Would you say your grief has felt overwhelming or unusually hard to bear?

I don't know about overwhelming. I mean... it's just hard. Losing a good friend is always going to be hard to bear, so I don't think there's anything unusual about it. It's just a very heavy sadness, but I wouldn't use a word like overwhelming. I'm just taking it one day at a time right now.
Has your grief made it hard for you to function in your day-to-day life?

Well, like I mentioned a minute ago... yes, it has. Since I'm retired, the church activities are a big part of my regular day, and I'm just not keeping up with them. Having to pass off the phone calls and the lists and the luncheon to the other members... that's a big change for me. I'm just not able to manage my usual routine the way I always did before.
Aside from the church responsibilities, do you feel your reaction has been more than what you would consider a normal grieving response to your friend's death?

No, I don't think so. I mean, it's just... I lost my best friend. I think anyone would be this sad. It's just a normal part of losing someone you care about so much. I don't feel like my reaction is out of the ordinary, just... just very sad.
Have the people close to you seemed to think your reaction is more than they would expect after your friend's death?

No, not that I've noticed. My family and the folks at church have just been really supportive. I think they all understand how close we were, so... no, nobody has said I'm reacting more than I should be. They just know I'm missing her.
